title: Natural piano players, early pay and Wiggles Pernell
summary: Gifted untrained pianists, his first date paying $1.25 and a Mobile gig for seven dollars, then Alton Pernell's brother.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: That's right, and my mother used to save the coupons from it. Oh yeah. But they used to have coupons with it, you know, along with the octagon soap and all that. And they used to have a mixture wherein they'd mix it up together and scrub the steps and naturally get through and then wash the sidewalks with the brick. And by the time the steps was dry and the red brick was dry it was just like this red rug sitting on the floor. Of course it wouldn't last very long depending on the time of the year it was and how much rain you would have. But naturally it would give it a very good setting and the aroma from the fish would give it a very good setting and more or less appetizing. And if you see it, you pass by it, you say, oh, this smells good, well we'll stop by and see. And then when you get inside, I mean there was so much going on that you would be glad to stay if you had any money in your pocket. You were going to stay for a while. And then the fellas would come by there from time to time and they would play. And one thing I had found in New Orleans, there was a whole lot of people that could always play the piano if they couldn't do anything else. They were more or less musically inclined people. And I wouldn't say that too much of them had training as far as learning music, but they were more or less gifted and they had the incentive to play, you know. That was natural music. Natural music and they played what they felt and not what they heard somebody else. You know they had their own ideas about it. And I have often wondered why a lot of people didn't spend too much time trying to cultivate the ideas, you know. But as I said before they were more or less happy-go-lucky people and they were just satisfied enough to have some place to stay and no food to eat and they were particularly satisfied. And the monies that they were getting, I wouldn't say that they were getting fabulous prices because I remember when I played my first date I worked for six hours for a dollar and a quarter. And when I got my best job I think I went with Sidney Dancefein and played a gig in Mobile, Alabama. Played one night in Mobile and we made seven dollars I think that night and I thought I was the richest person in the world. Well it just goes to show you, you know. Of course I was in school at the time. But lots of times even if we didn't get anything we were satisfied just to know that we could play and we enjoyed playing and I've always worked with a bunch of fellas that enjoyed playing. And it's like I went to see a buddy of mine and I felt terribly sorry about him. I don't know whether you had the occasion to meet him or not but he had played around New Orleans for quite some time. As a matter of fact we worked together in Sidney Dancefein's band and his name was, we used to call him Wiggles. Did you know Alton who plays piano?
